questions: Should the function handle tuples of varying lengths, and if so, how should missing values be represented (e.g., NaN, dropping rows, padding)?
What should happen if the input list is empty? Should it return an empty DataFrame or raise an error?
Are the elements in the tuples guaranteed to be numeric (int/float), or should other types (e.g., strings, complex numbers) be handled gracefully?
Should the DataFrame columns be labeled (e.g., with default integer indices or custom names), or is the labeling unspecified?
Is the order of rows in the DataFrame required to match the order of tuples in the input list exactly?
Should the function preserve the original tuple structure (e.g., nested tuples) or flatten them before applying sine?
What is the expected behavior if a tuple element is None or NaN? Should sine be applied, skipped, or result in an error?
Should the function modify the input list or tuples in any way, or ensure immutability?
